sanskrit: saṁ jāgṛvadbhir jaramāṇa idhyate dame damūnā iṣayann iḻas pade | viśvasya hotā haviṣo vareṇyo vibhur vibhāvā suṣakhā sakhīyate ||
english: He is kindled together with the wakeful ones, waxing old in the house, the house-lord quickening at the station of Iḷā; the Hotṛ of all, most worthy of the oblation, all-pervading, radiant — as a true friend he is befriended.

sanskrit: sa darśataśrīr atithir gṛhe-gṛhe vane-vane śiśriye takvavīr iva | janaṁ-janaṁ janyo nāti manyate viśa ā kṣeti viśyo viśaṁ-viśam ||
english: He of splendid beauty, a guest in every house, nestles in every forest like a swift hawk; he, the people's own, does not despise any folk, but dwells among the clans — a clansman among every clan.

sanskrit: sudakṣo dakṣaiḥ kratunāsi sukratur agne kaviḥ kāvyenāsi viśvavit | vasur vasūnāṁ kṣayasi tvam eka id dyāvā ca yāni pṛthivī ca puṣyataḥ ||
english: O Agni, expert among experts by your power of discernment, you are of excellent will; a seer by your wisdom, you know all things. You alone, O treasure among treasures, are lord of whatever Heaven and Earth cherish.

sanskrit: prajānann agne tava yonim ṛtviyam iḻāyas pade ghṛtavantam āsadaḥ | ā te cikitra uṣasām ivetayo 'repasaḥ sūryasyeva raśmayaḥ ||
english: Knowing, O Agni, your timely birthplace — the butter-rich station of Iḷā — you have been set in place; your gleaming rays have become visible, like the dawns, blameless, like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tava śriyo varṣyasyeva vidyutaś citrāś cikitra uṣasāṁ na ketavaḥ ||yad oṣadhīr abhisṛṣṭo vanāni ca pari svayaṁ cinuṣe annam āsye ||
english: Your splendours flash like lightning of the rain-cloud; wondrous, they appear like the banners of the Dawns. When you are sent forth among the plants and forests, you gather your own food into your mouth.

sanskrit: tam oṣadhīr dadhire garbham ṛtviyaṁ tam āpo agniṁ janayanta mātaraḥ | tam it samānaṁ vaninaś ca vīrudho 'ntarvatīś ca suvate ca viśvahā ||
english: Him — Agni — the plants bore as their timely embryo; him the waters, like mothers, brought forth; him, ever the same one, the trees and herbs, those pregnant and those giving birth, perpetually deliver.

sanskrit: vātopadhūta iṣito vaśāṁ anu tṛṣu yad annā veviṣad vitiṣṭhase | ā te yatante rathyo yathā pṛthak śardhāṁsy agne ajarāṇi dhakṣataḥ ||
english: Fan-fanned by the wind, impelled, you spread yourself following the dry fuel, flashing swiftly through the food; your un-aging hosts rush at you separately, like charioteers, O Agni, blazing.

sanskrit: medhākāraṁ vidathasya prasādhanam agniṁ hotāram paribhūtamamam matim | tam id arbhe haviṣy ā samānam it tam in mahe vṛṇate nānyaṁ tvat ||
english: Agni the author of wisdom, the adornment of the assembly, the Hotṛ, most pre-eminent, most inspired — him alone they choose for the small oblation, and him alone they choose for the great sacrifice — none other than you.

sanskrit: tvām id atra vṛṇate tvāyavo hotāram agne vidatheṣu vedhasaḥ | yad devayanto dadhati prayāṁsi te haviṣmanto manavo vṛktabarhiṣaḥ ||
english: You alone they choose here, the devotees of you, O Agni, as Hotṛ among the wise in the assemblies; when the god-worshipping Manus, possessing oblations, with trimmed grass-strewings, lay down offerings before you.

sanskrit: tavāgne hotraṁ tava potram ṛtviyaṁ tava neṣṭraṁ tvam agnid ṛtāyataḥ | tava praśāstraṁ tvam adhvarīyasi brahmā cāsi gṛhapatiś ca no dame ||
english: Yours, O Agni, is the office of Hotṛ; yours, seasonally, that of Potṛ; yours is the role of Neṣṭṛ; you are the Agnīdh for the truth-striving; yours is the Praśāstṛ's part; you act as the Adhvaryu, and you are also the Brahmán and the householder in our home.

sanskrit: yas tubhyam agne amṛtāya martyas samidhā dāśad uta vā haviṣkṛti | tasya hotā bhavasi yāsi dūtyam upa brūṣe yajasy adhvarīyasi ||
english: Whatever mortal, O Agni, for immortality's sake presents you with fuel or with the making of oblation — for him you become the Hotṛ, you go on the messenger's errand, you address him, you sacrifice, you perform the adhvara.

sanskrit: imā asmai matayo vāco asmad āṁ ṛco giraḥ suṣṭutayaḥ sam agmata | vasūyavo vasave jātavedase vṛddhāsu cid vardhano yāsu cākanat ||
english: These thoughts, these words from us, these hymns, praises, and songs of eulogy have assembled together for him, desiring wealth, for Vasu, for Jātavedas — he who grows by each increase and who has delighted in them.

sanskrit: imām pratnāya suṣṭutiṁ navīyasīṁ voceya asmā uśate śṛṇotu naḥ | bhūyā antarā hṛdy asya nispṛśe jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ ||
english: This newest eulogy I would speak for the Ancient one, who yearns — let him hear us. May it touch deeply within his heart, like a well-dressed, loving wife close to her husband.

sanskrit: yasminn aśvāsa ṛṣabhāsa ukṣaṇo vaśā meṣā avasṛṣṭāsa āhutāḥ | kīlālapaṁ somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase hṛdā matiṁ janaye cārum agnaye ||
english: For him in whom horses, bulls, oxen, cows, and rams are released and offered as oblations — for the drinker of sweet drink, for the Soma-backed wise one — I generate from my heart a beautiful hymn for Agni.

sanskrit: ahāvy agne havir āsye te srucīva ghṛtaṁ camvīva somaḥ | vājasaniṁ rayim asme suvīram praśastaṁ dhehi yaśasaṁ bṛhantam ||
english: O Agni, the oblation is to be placed in your mouth — clarified butter as in the ladle, Soma as in the pressing-bowl. Grant us a prize-winning wealth, with excellent heroes, famed and glorious, and great.

sanskrit: yajñasya vo rathyaṁ viśpatiṁ viśāṁ hotāram akthor atithiṁ vibhāvasum | śocañ chuṣkāsu hariṇīṣu jarbhurad vṛṣā ketur yajato dyām aśāyata ||
english: I praise for you the chariot-driver of the sacrifice, the lord of the peoples, the Hotṛ of the nights, the guest rich in light; blazing, roaring upon the dry tawny ones, the virile one, the banner-fire, the adorable, has stretched himself across the sky.

sanskrit: imam añjaspām ubhaye akṛṇvata dharmāṇam agniṁ vidathasya sādhanam | aktuṁ na yahvam uṣasaḥ purohitaṁ tanūnapātam aruṣasya niṁsate ||
english: Both groups — gods and mortals — have made him the universal one, Agni, the establishing law of the assembly, its practitioner; like the ancient night of the Dawns, the purohita, Tanūnapāt of the ruddy one, they lick him.

sanskrit: baḻ asya nīthā vi paṇeś ca manmahe vayā asya prahutā āsur attave | yadā ghorāso amṛtatvam āśatād ij janasya daivyasya carkiran ||
english: We celebrate his leadership and also the merchants' thought; his branches, well-offered, are for eating. When the terrible ones have attained immortality, they revolve perpetually then among the divine folk.

sanskrit: ṛtasya hi prasitir dyaur uru vyaco namo mahy aramatir panīyasī | indro mitro varuṇas saṁ cikitrire 'tho bhagaḥ savitā pūdadakṣasaḥ ||
english: For Heaven, the wide expanse, is the outlet of Ṛta; the great Aramatī is the more wondrous worship; Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa have recognised each other, and also Bhaga and Savitṛ who bestows pure power.

sanskrit: pra rudreṇa yayinā yanti sindhavas tiro mahīm aramatim dadhanvire | yebhiḥ parijmā pariyann uru jrayo vi roruvaj jaṭhare viśvam ukṣate ||
english: With Rudra the rapid one, the rivers flow onward; they have run across the great Aramatī. By those with whom the encircler roams the wide expanse, roaring everywhere, he sprinkles everything in his belly.

sanskrit: krāṇā rudrā maruto viśvakṛṣṭayo divaḥ śyenāso asurasya nīḻayaḥ | tebhiś caṣṭe varuṇo mitro aryam endro devebhir arvaśebhir arvaśaḥ ||
english: Active, the Rudras, the Maruts of all peoples, the eagles of the sky, the nestlings of the Asura — together with them Varuṇa surveys, and Mitra, Aryaman, and Indra with the swift gods, himself swift.

sanskrit: indre bhujaṁ śaśamānāsa āśata sūro dṛśīke vṛṣaṇaś ca pauṁsye | pra ye nv asyārhaṇā tatakṣire yujaṁ vajraṁ nṛṣadaneṣu kāravāḥ ||
english: Those who have toiled have reached their enjoyment in Indra — the hero in his aspect, and the bulls in their virility. The skilled singers who now have fashioned his fitting token, the companion-bolt, for the seats of men.

sanskrit: sūraś cid ā harito asya rīramad indrād ā kaś cid bhayate tavīyasaḥ | bhīmasya vṛṣṇo jaṭharād abhiśvaso dive-dive sahuriḥ stann abādhitaḥ ||
english: Even the sun's tawny mares have been held back by him; who from Indra the mightier does not fear? From the belly of the fearful bull the mighty roar thunders day by day, unhindered.

sanskrit: stomaṁ vo adya rudrāya śikvase kṣayadvīrāya namasā didiṣṭana | yebhiḥ śivaḥ svavāṁ evayāvabhir divaḥ siṣakti svayaśā nikāmabhiḥ ||
english: Aim today with homage a hymn for Rudra the able, the lord of heroes; through whose benevolent, self-luminous swift ones he pursues the sky according to desire, of his own fame.

sanskrit: te hi prajāyā abharanta vi śravo bṛhaspatiṁ vṛṣabhaḥ somajāmayaḥ | yajñair atharvā prathamo vi dhārayad devā dakṣair bhṛgavaḥ saṁ cikitrire ||
english: They have spread fame far for offspring — Bṛhaspati the bull, the Soma-kindred ones; Atharvan by sacrifices first sustained them; the gods and the Bhṛgus have come together through their powers.

sanskrit: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūriretasā narāśaṁsas caturaṅgo yamo 'ditiḥ | devas tvaṣṭā draviṇodā ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ pra rodasī maruto viṣṇur arhire ||
english: Indeed Heaven and Earth with their abundant seed, Narāśaṁsa of four forms, Yama, Aditi, the god Tvaṣṭṛ, Draviṇodas, Ṛbhukṣan — the Maruts and Viṣṇu have honoured both worlds.

sanskrit: uta sya na uśijām urviyā kavir ahiḥ śṛṇotu budhnyo havīmani | sūryāmāsā vicarantā divikṣitā dhiyā śamīnahuṣī asya bodhatam ||
english: And let that far-famed seer of the Uśijas, Ahi Budhnya, hear our invocation; let the Sun and Moon roaming the sky, dwellers in heaven, both understand this sacrifice by their wisdom — Nahuṣī among the workers.

sanskrit: pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṁ viśvadevyo 'pāṁ napād avatu vāyur iṣṭaye | ātmānaṁ vasyo abhi vātam arcata tad aśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutam ||
english: May Pūṣan of all the gods further our journey; may Apāṁ Napāt protect for the offering; sing the self-sustaining Wind with better songs — you two Aśvins, easy to invoke, hear this at your going.

sanskrit: viśām āsām abhayānām adhikṣitaṁ gīrbhir u svayaśasaṁ gṛṇīmasi | gnābhir viśvābhir aditim anarvaṇam aktor yuvānaṁ nṛmaṇā adhā patim ||
english: Him, the lord of these fearless peoples, self-glorious, we praise with songs; Aditi along with all the divine women, un-assailed — the young lord of heroes, the night's master.

sanskrit: rebhad atra januṣā pūrvo aṅgirā grāvāṇa ūrdhvā abhi cakṣur adhvaram | yebhir vihāyā abhavad vicakṣaṇaḥ pāthaḥ sumekaṁ svadhitir vanavnati ||
english: Here the ancient Aṅgiras sang from birth; the pressing-stones raised high look upon the rite; through which the far-seer gained the sky, the path is firm, the self-sharpened axe at work in the wood-bearing one.

sanskrit: mahi dyāvāpṛthivī bhūtam urvī nārī yahvī na rodasī sadaṁ naḥ | tebhir naḥ pātaṁ sahyasa ebhir naḥ pātaṁ śūṣaṇi ||
english: Be great and wide for us, O Heaven and Earth, like two young women, the two great Rodases always with us; protect us with them from the powerful, protect us with them in battle.

sanskrit: yajñe-yajñe sa martyo devān saparyati | yaḥ sumnair dīrghaśruttama āvivāsaty enān ||
english: That mortal in every sacrifice serves the gods — he who, with good thoughts, the most far-famed, approaches them with homage.

sanskrit: viśveṣām irajyavo devānāṁ vār mahaḥ | viśve hi viśvamahaso viśve yajñeṣu yajñiyāḥ ||
english: The generosity of all the gods is the best great gift; for the All-gods, mighty all of them, are all worthy of sacrifice at every sacrifice.

sanskrit: te ghā rājāno amṛtasya mandrā aryamā mitro varuṇaḥ parijmā | kad rudro nṛṇāṁ stuto marutaḥ pūṣaṇo bhagaḥ ||
english: Those kings of immortality — the delightful ones — Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa the encircler; where is Rudra, lauded of men; the Maruts, Pūṣan, Bhaga?

sanskrit: uta no naktam apāṁ vṛṣaṇvasū sūryāmāsā sadanāya sadhanyā | sacā yat sādy eṣām ahir budhneṣu budhnyaḥ ||
english: And by night, both rich in bull-power — Sun and Moon, home-companions, for our dwelling; when Ahi Budhnya settles among these at the foundations, primordial.

sanskrit: uta no devāv aśvinā śubhas patī dhāmabhir mitrāvaruṇā uruṣyatām | mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate 'ti dhanveva duritā ||
english: And may the two divine Aśvins, lords of beauty, and Mitra-Varuṇa with their forms protect us widely; he reaches great wealth — passing over difficulties as if a desert.

sanskrit: uta no rudrā cin mṛḻatām aśvinā viśve devāso rathaspatiṁ bhagaḥ | ṛbhur vāja ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ parijmā viśvavedasaḥ ||
english: And may even the Rudras be gracious to us, the Aśvins, all the gods, the lord of the chariot, Bhaga; Ṛbhu, Vāja, Ṛbhukṣan, the encircler, the all-knowing ones.

sanskrit: ṛbhur ṛbhukṣā ṛbhur vidhato mada ā te harī jūjuvāṇasya vājinā | duṣṭaraṁ yasya sāma cid ṛdhag yajño na māṇuṣaḥ ||
english: Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣā, Ṛbhu — the joy of the devout; your two bay coursers, O swift-running one; whose chant alone is hard to surpass, whose sacrifice is set apart from all human ones.

sanskrit: kṛdhī no ahrayo deva savitaḥ sa ca stuṣe maghonām | saho na indro vahnibhir ny eṣāṁ carṣaṇīnāṁ cakraṁ raśmiṁ na yoyuve ||
english: Make us blameless, divine Savitṛ — he who is praised among the lords of bounty; like Indra with the carriers, he has rolled the wheel of these clans like a rein.

sanskrit: aiṣu dyāvāpṛthivī dhātam mad asme vīreṣu viśvacarṣaṇi śravaḥ | pṛkṣaṁ vājasya sātaye pṛkṣaṁ rāyota turvaṇe ||
english: Set for us, O Heaven and Earth, joy among our heroes — fame perceived by all peoples; strength for winning the prize, strength also for overcoming wealth in the contest.

sanskrit: etaṁ śaṁsam indrāsmayuṣ tvaṁ kūcit santaṁ sahasāvann abhiṣṭaye | sadā pāhy abhiṣṭaye medatāṁ vedatā vaso ||
english: This praise, O mighty Indra who yearns for us, wherever it may be, protect for victory; protect always for victory — may the joyous one find it, O Vasu.

sanskrit: etam me stomaṁ tanā na sūrye dyutadyāmānaṁ vāvṛdhanta nṛṇām | saṁvananam nāśvyaṁ taṣṭevānapacyutam ||
english: This hymn of mine, stretched out as a cord in the sun, shining day by day, men have made grow; it is a charm for concord, not horse-like, carved like a carpenter's work, unshaken.

sanskrit: vāvarta yeṣāṁ rāyā yuktaiṣāṁ hiraṇyayī | nemodhaditā na pauṁsyā vṛtheva viṣṭāntā ||
english: He has turned toward those whose wealth is yoked together — golden wealth; not weakened in mind, not unmanly, not extended uselessly as though spread about in vain.

sanskrit: pra tad duḥśīme pṛthavāne vene pra rāme vocam asure maghavatsv | ye yuktvāya pañca śatāsmayupa pathā viśrāvy eṣām ||
english: That I would proclaim for Duḥśīman, Pṛthavāna, and Vena; I would proclaim it for Rāma among the powerful asuras — those who, for the harnessing, possess five hundred attendants — may their path be renowned.

sanskrit: adhīn nv atra saptatiṁ ca sapta ca | sadyo didiṣṭa tānvaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa pārthyaḥ sadyo didiṣṭa māyavaḥ ||
english: Here indeed I have perceived seventy and seven; Tānva shone forth at once, Pārthya shone forth at once, Māyava shone forth at once.

sanskrit: praite vadantu pra vayaṁ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṁ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ | yad adrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākam āśavaḥ ślokaṁ ghoṣam bharathendrāya sominaḥ ||
english: Let them speak forth; we shall speak too — to the pressing-stones from those that speak, to those that speak. When the rocks, the mountains together, swift ones, carry the resonance and sound, O Soma-bearers, to Indra.

sanskrit: ete vadanti śatavat sahasravad abhi krandanti haritebhir āsabhiḥ | viṣṭvī grāvāṇaḥ sukṛtaḥ sukṛtyayā hotuś cit pūrve haviradhyam āśata ||
english: These speak a hundredfold, a thousandfold; they cry out with their tawny mouths; the pressing-stones stretched out, well-wrought by their good craft, first eagerly eat even the Hotṛ's food.

sanskrit: ete vadanty avidann anā madhu ny ūṅkhayante adhi pakva āmiṣi | vṛkṣasya śākhām aruṇasya bapsatas te sūbharvā vṛṣabhāḥ prem arāviṣuḥ ||
english: These speak out; they have found honey for the bowl; they swing down upon the cooked raw flesh. They — the bulls, gleaming-toothed — cried out eagerly while devouring the branch of the ruddy tree.

sanskrit: bṛhad vadanti madirenena mandinendra kṛośanto 'vidann anā madhu | saṁrabhyā dhīrāḥ svasṛbhir anartiṣur āghoṣayantaḥ pṛthivīm upadbibhiḥ ||
english: They speak greatly, gladdened by the intoxicant, crying out; they have found honey for the bowl of Indra, the gladdening one; the wise ones, clasping one another, leaping with their sisters, have made the earth resound with their stamps.

sanskrit: suparṇā vācam akratopadyavy ākhare kṛṣṇā iṣirā anartiṣuḥ | nyaṅ niyanti uparasya niṣkṛtam purū reto dadhire sūryaśvitaḥ ||
english: The fair-winged ones, the black, lively ones, made speech in the air-hole of the nether stone; they guide downward the product of the upper stone; the sun-white ones have deposited abundant seed.

sanskrit: ugrā iva pravahantaḥ samāyamuḥ sākaṁ yuktā vṛṣaṇo bibhrato dhuraḥ | yac chvasanto jagrasāṇā arāviṣuḥ śṛṇva eṣām prothatho arvatām iva ||
english: Like fierce ones flowing forth they came together, yoked bulls bearing the yoke together; as they breathed and swallowed they cried out — you can hear the neighing of them like that of horses.

sanskrit: daśāvanibhyo daśakakṣyebhyo daśayoktrebhyo daśayojanebhyaḥ | daśābhīśubhyo arcatājarebhyo daśa dhuro daśa yuktā vahadbhyaḥ ||
english: Ten coursers, ten girths, ten yoke-ropes, ten distances, ten reins — praise the un-aging ones; ten shafts, ten harnessed ones that carry.

sanskrit: te adrayaḥ daśayantrāsa āśavas teṣām ādhānam pary eti haryatam | ta ū sutasya somyasyāndhaso 'ṁśoḥ pīyūṣam prathamasya bhejire ||
english: These rocks, ten-controlled, swift — their support goes around adorable; they indeed have partaken of the first milky sap of the pressed Soma shoot, the Soma plant.

sanskrit: te somādo harī indrasya niṁsate 'ṁśuṁ duhanto adhy āsate gavi | tebhir dugdham papivān somyam madhv indro vardhate prathate vṛṣāyate ||
english: They, the Soma-drinkers, lick Indra's two bays; milking the shoot they sit upon the cow. By what is milked by them — having drunk the Soma-sweet honey — Indra grows, expands, exerts himself as a bull.

sanskrit: vṛṣā vo aṁśur na kilā riṣāthaneḻāvantaḥ sadam it stha ṭanāśitāḥ | raivatevamahasā cāravāḥ sthana yasya grāvāṇo ajuṣadhvam adhvaram ||
english: The shoot is your bull — you shall not indeed be harmed, O praise-possessing ones, always feeding from the bowl; with the majesty of one rich in gifts you are lovely — you whose pressing-stones have served the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tṛdilā atṛdilāso adrayo 'śramaṇā aśṛthitā amṛtyavaḥ | anāturā ajarāḥ sthāmaviṣṇavaḥ supīvaso atṛṣitā atṛṣṇajaḥ ||
english: With holes, without holes — these rocks are unwearied, unloosened, immortal; not ailing, not aging, all-pervading by their power, well-rounded, never thirsty, unborn of thirst.

sanskrit: dhruvā eva vaḥ pitaro yuge-yuge kṣemakāmāsaḥ sadaso na yuñjate | ajuryāso hariṣāco haridrava ā dyāṁ raveṇa pṛthivīm aśuśravuḥ ||
english: Firm, like your fathers age after age, desiring safety, they do not yoke to the seat; ever-young, swallowing tawny ones, of tawny colour, they have resounded to heaven and earth with their cry.

sanskrit: tad id vadanty adrayovimocaneyāmann añjaspā iva ghed upadbibhiḥ | vapanto bījam iva dhānyākṛtaḥ pṛñcanti somaṁ na minanti bapsataḥ ||
english: That the rocks speak out at the unharnessing as on the journey — like drinkers of the ointment, indeed, with their thumps; sowing seed like grain-workers, they mix the Soma but do not diminish it in their devouring.

sanskrit: sute adhvare adhi vācam akratā krīḻayo na mātaram tudantaḥ | vi ṣū muñcā suṣuvuṣo manīṣāṁ vi vartantām adraya cāyamānāḥ ||
english: At the pressed sacrifice they have made speech over it — playing ones, striking like a mother; release the thought of those that have pressed well; let the stones revolve as they resound.

sanskrit: haye jāye manasā tiṣṭha ghore vacāṁsi miśrā kṛṇavāvahai nu | na nau mantrā anuditāsa ete mayas karan paratare ca nāhan ||
english: O wife, linger a while with me in heart, O terrible one; let us now mingle our words together. These our mutual counsels, once spoken, will not bring happiness on another day beyond.

sanskrit: kim etā vācā kṛṇavā tavāham prākramiṣam uṣasām agriveva | purūrava punar astam parehi durāpanā vātaivāham asmi ||
english: What shall I do with this speech of yours? I have stepped forth like the foremost of the dawns. O Purūravas, go back home again; I am as hard to catch as the wind.

sanskrit: iṣur na śriya iṣudher asanā goṣāḥ śatasā na raṁhiḥ | avīre kratau vi davidyutan norā na māyuṁ citayanta dhunayaḥ ||
english: Like an arrow from the quiver shot for beauty, winning cattle, swift as a hundred — in the will of the powerless one they flashed, but the shakers did not notice the bleat of the ewe.

sanskrit: sā vasu dadhatī śvaśurāya vaya uṣo yadi vaṣṭy antige gṛhāt | astaṁ nanakṣe yasmiñ cākan divā naktaṁ śnathitā vaitasena ||
english: She who brings treasure — providing sustenance to the father-in-law — O Uṣas, if she desires a home close by; she has reached the home where she took delight, pierced day and night by one of reed.

sanskrit: triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitaseno uta sma me 'vyatyai pṛṇāsi | purūravo anu te ketam āyaṁ rājā me vīra tanvas tad āsīḥ ||
english: Three times a day the Vaitasena would strike me, and you would fill me also insatiably; I came after your sign, O Purūravas — you were a king among heroes, the soul of my body.

sanskrit: yā sujūrṇiḥ śreṇiḥ sumnaāpir hradecakṣur na granthivīṁ caranyuḥ | tā añjayo 'ruṇayo na sasruḥ śriye gāvo na dhenavo 'navanta ||
english: Those well-adorned ones, in rows, winning favour, their eyes like a lake — roaming, not knotted — those tawny anointings have flowed; like cows and milk-cows they have lowed for beauty.

sanskrit: sam asmij jāyamāna āsata gnā utem avardhan nadyaḥ svagūrtāḥ | mahe yat tvā purūravo raṇāyāvardhayan dasyu hatyāya devāḥ ||
english: Together with this one being born, the divine women sat — and the self-welcome rivers made him grow; when, O Purūravas, for great joy, the gods made you grow for the slaying of the Dasyus.

sanskrit: sacā yad āsu jahatīṣv atkam amānuṣīṣu māṇuṣo niṣeve | apa sma mat tarasantī na bhujyus tā atrasan rathaspṛśo nāśvāḥ ||
english: When a human man dwells among those non-human ones, leaving his cloak among them; like Bhujyu flying away from me — they trembled, those touching the chariot, like horses.

sanskrit: yad āsu marto amṛtāsu nispṛk saṁ kṣoṇibhiḥ kratubhir na pṛṅkte | tā ātayo na tanvaḥ śumbhata svā aśvāso na krīḻayo dandaśānāḥ ||
english: When a mortal intermingles with the immortal ones and does not combine his deeds with theirs; those flowing ones adorn their own bodies — like biting horses, they play.

sanskrit: vidyun na yā patatī davidyod bharantī me apyā kāmyāni | janiṣṭo apo naryaḥ sujātaḥ prorvaśī tirata dīrgham āyuḥ ||
english: She who flashed like a darting lightning, bringing to me the things I yearn for, close to the waters — a hero was born, well-born; let Urvaśī extend long life.

sanskrit: jajñiṣa itthā gopīthyāya hi dadhātha tat purūravo ma ojaḥ | aśāsaṁ tvā viduṣī sasminn ahan na ma āśṛṇo kim abhug vadāsi ||
english: You were born indeed for protection; you have placed that strength in me, O Purūravas. I, knowing, instructed you on that very day; you did not listen to me — what do you say you have not enjoyed?

sanskrit: kadā sūnuḥ pitaraṁ jāta icchāc cakran nāśru vartayad vijānan | ko dampatī samanasā vi yūyod adha yad agniḥ śvaśureṣu dīdayat ||
english: When will the son, being born, seek his father? He will shed tears, knowing. Who would separate a couple of one mind, when Agni shines among the parents-in-law?

sanskrit: prati bravāṇi vartayate aśru cakran na krandad ādhye śivāyai | pra tat te hinavā yat te asme parehy astaṁ nahi mūra māpaḥ ||
english: I will speak in answer — the tear rolls — he shall not weep like a wheel for an auspicious wife; I shall send you forth that which belongs to you among us — go home, O fool, do not perish.

sanskrit: sudevo adya prapaṭed anāvṛt parāvataṁ paramāṁ gantavā u | adhā śayīta nirṛter upasthe 'dainaṁ vṛkā rabhasāso adyuḥ ||
english: The god-blessed one today may rush off, not returning, to go to the remotest distance; then he would lie in the lap of Nirṛti — then the fierce wolves would devour him.

sanskrit: purūravo mā mṛthā mā pra papto mā tvā vṛkāso aśivāsa u kṣan | na vai straiṇāni sakhyāni santi sālāvṛkāṇāṁ hṛdayāny etā ||
english: O Purūravas, do not die; do not fall; let not the un-gracious wolves devour you; there are truly no friendships with women — the hearts of these are the hearts of jackals.

sanskrit: yad virūpācaram martyeṣv avasaṁ rātrīḥ śaradaś catasraḥ | ghṛtasya stokaṁ sakṛd ahna āśnāṁ tād evedaṁ tātṛpāṇā carāmi ||
english: When, changed in form, I lived among mortals, spending the nights through four autumns, eating a drop of ghee once a day — it is with this satisfaction that I still wander thus.

sanskrit: antarikṣaprāṁ rajaso vimānīm upa śikṣāmy urvaśīṁ vasiṣṭhaḥ | upa tvā rātiḥ sukṛtasya tiṣṭhān ni vartasva hṛdayaṁ tapyate me ||
english: I, Vasiṣṭha, seek to learn from Urvaśī who fills the atmosphere, who measures the realm of space. May the gift of good deeds stand near you — turn back; my heart is burning.

sanskrit: iti tvā devā ima āhur aiḷa yathem etad bhavasi mṛtyubandhuḥ | prajā te devān haviṣā yajāti svarga u tvam api mādayāse ||
english: Thus these gods say to you, O son of Iḷā, even as you are here a kinsman of death: your offspring shall sacrifice to the gods with oblation, and you yourself shall also rejoice in heaven.

sanskrit: pra te mahe vidathe śaṁsiṣaṁ harī pra te vanve vanuṣo haryatam madam | ghṛtaṁ na yo haribhiś cāru secata ā tvā viśantu harivarpasaṁ giraḥ ||
english: For you, great one, at the assembly I have proclaimed your two bays; I have praised to the worshipper your beautiful, bay-coloured joy; you who shed welcome clarified butter with your bays — may my songs enter into you of bay form.

sanskrit: hariṁ hi yonim abhi ye samasvaraṁ hinvanto harī divyaṁ yathā sadaḥ | ā yam pṛṇanti haribhir na dhenava indrāya śūṣaṁ harivantam arcata ||
english: Those who with one voice together urge the bay toward the bay womb, as toward the heavenly seat; whom the milk-cows fill as with the bays — sing to Indra the bay-possessing might.

sanskrit: so asya vajro harito ya āyaso harir nikāmo harir ā gabhastyoḥ | dyumnī suśipro harimanyusāyaka indre ni rūpā haritā mimikṣire ||
english: His bolt is tawny, of iron; tawny is his desire, tawny in his two fists; radiant, fair-jawed, with tawny-anger dart — in Indra the tawny forms have been instilled.

sanskrit: divi na ketur adhi dhāyi haryato vivyacad vajro harito na raṁhyā | tudad ahiṁ hariśipro ya āyasaḥ sahasraśokā abhavad dharimbharaḥ ||
english: Like a banner in the sky the bay one has been set; the tawny bolt has spread like swift arrows; the iron, bay-jawed one who smote the serpent became he who bears the bay — with a thousand flames.

sanskrit: tvaṁ-tvam aharyathā upastutaḥ pūrvebhir indra harikeśa yajvabhiḥ | tvaṁ haryasi tava viśvam ukthyam asāmi rādho harijāta haryatam ||
english: You, ever you, O bay-maned Indra, are praised, worshipped by former sacrificers; you love bay things, all praise is yours — the ungiven bounty of the bay-born, the lovely one.

sanskrit: tā vajriṇam mandinaṁ stomyam madam indraṁ rathe vahato haryatā harī | purūṇy asmai savanāni haryata indrāya somā harayo dadhanvire ||
english: The two lovely bays carry in the chariot Indra, the wielder of the bolt, the glad, the laudable joy; many pressings are lovely for him — the Soma-bays have run for Indra.

sanskrit: araṁ kāmāya harayo dadhanvire sthirāya hinvan harayo harī turā | arvadbhir yo haribhir joṣam īyate so asya kāmaṁ harivantam ānaśe ||
english: The bays have run fit for desire; urging the steady one, the two swift bays go; he who goes with pleasure with the bay coursers — he has reached his bay-coloured desire.

sanskrit: hariśmaśāruṁ harikeśa āyasas turaspeche yo haripā avardhata | arvadbhir yo haribhir vājinīvasur ati viśvā duritā pāriṣad dharī ||
english: Bay-bearded, bay-maned, iron, at the quick draft he who is a bay-drinker has grown; he whose two bays with prize-winning wealth in coursers — may he pass beyond all difficulties.

sanskrit: sruveva yasya hariṇī vipetatu śipre vājāya hariṇī davidhvataḥ | pra yat kṛte camase marmṛjad dharī pītvā madasya haryatasyāndhsaḥ ||
english: Whose two tawny jaws flew up like ladles, the two tawny ones flashing for the prize; when having drunk of the lovely intoxicating juice, the two bays polished the made bowl.

sanskrit: uta sma sadma haryatasya pastyor atyo na vājaṁ harivāṁ acikradat | mahī cid dhi dhiṣaṇāharyad ojasā bṛhad vayo dadhiṣe haryataś cid ā ||
english: And the dwelling of the lovely one in the folds echoed — the bay-possessing one shouted for the prize like a racing horse; for the great power-goddess longed for it by force; you have placed great sustenance from the lovely one.

sanskrit: ā rodasī haryamāṇo mahitvā navyaṁ-navyaṁ haryasi manma nu priyam | pra pastyam asura haryataṁ gor āviṣ kṛdhi haraye sūryāya ||
english: Filling both worlds by your greatness, O one delighted by bays, you love ever-new beloved hymns; make manifest the lovely dwelling of the cow, O Asura, for bay Sūrya.

sanskrit: ā tvā haryantam prayujo janānāṁ rathe vahantu hariśipram indra | pibā yathā pratibhṛtasya madhvo haryan yajñaṁ sadhamāde daśoṇim ||
english: Let the impellers of men carry you, bay-delighted, on your chariot, bay-jawed Indra; drink, as you love it, of the brought mead — loving the sacrifice, at the common joy feast, at the ten-fold pressing.

sanskrit: apāḥ pūrvesāṁ harivaḥ sutānām atho idaṁ savanaṁ kevalaṁ te | mamadhhi somam madhumantam indra satrā vṛṣañ jaṭhara ā vṛṣasva ||
english: You have drunk of the former pressings, O bay-possessing one; now this pressing is entirely yours; drink the sweet Soma, O Indra — O bull, fill yourself completely in your belly.

sanskrit: yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyas triyugam purā | manai nu babhrūṇām ahaṁ śataṁ dhāmāni sapta ca ||
english: The plants that were born of old, three ages before the gods — I shall meditate upon the hundred and seven abodes of those tawny ones.

sanskrit: śataṁ vo amba dhāmāni sahasram uta vo ruhaḥ | adhā śatakratvo yūyam imam me agadaṁ kṛta ||
english: A hundred are your abodes, O mothers, a thousand your growths; make this man of mine free from disease, you of a hundred powers.

sanskrit: oṣadhīḥ prati modadhvaṁ puṣpavatīḥ prasūvarīḥ | aśvā iva sajitvāvarir vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇavaḥ ||
english: Rejoice, O plants, you that are flowering and fruitful; like mares that conquer together, the herbs, those that carry across.

sanskrit: oṣadhīr iti mātaras tad vo devīr upa bruve | saneya aśvaṁ gāṁ vāsa ātmānaṁ tava pūruṣa ||
english: O plants, you who are mothers — the divine ones — I invoke you as such; may I gain a horse, a cow, a garment — and your own life-force, O man.

sanskrit: aśvatthe vo niṣadanam parne vo vasatiṣ kṛtā | gobhāja it kilāsatha yat sanavatha pūruṣam ||
english: Your resting place is in the Aśvattha tree, your dwelling has been made in the Parṇa leaf; you are truly sharers in cattle when you win the man.

sanskrit: yatrauṣadhīḥ samagatā rājānaḥ samitāv iva | vipraḥ sa ucyate bhiṣag rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ ||
english: Where the plants have assembled like kings in a council — that inspired one is called a healer, a slayer of demons, a dispeller of disease.

sanskrit: aśvāvatīṁ somāvatīm ūrjayantīm udojasam | āvitsi sarvā oṣadhīr asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: I have found all the plants — those rich in horses, rich in Soma, enlivening, full of vigour — for his uninjured well-being.

sanskrit: uc chuṣmā oṣadhīnāṁ gāvo goṣṭhād iverate | dhanaṁ saniṣyantīnām ātmānaṁ tava pūruṣa ||
english: The vigours of the plants go up like cows from the cow-pen; those that shall win wealth — and your own self, O man.

sanskrit: iṣkṛtir nāma vo mātāthoyūyaṁ stha niṣkṛtīḥ | sīrāḥ patraviṇīḥ sthana yad āmayati niṣ kṛtha ||
english: Your mother is called Iṣkṛti, and you are the cleansers; you are the running ones, the wing-bearing ones — what ails, you cleanse away.

sanskrit: ati viśvāḥ pariṣṭhāḥ stena iva vrajaṁ akramuḥ | oṣadhīḥ prācucyavur yat kiṁ ca tanvor rapaḥ ||
english: Beyond all enclosures they have stepped like a thief toward the fold; the plants have shaken loose whatever ailment afflicts the body.

sanskrit: yad imā vājayann aham oṣadhīḥ hasta āda dhe | ātmā yakṣmasya naśyati purā jīvagṛbho yathā ||
english: When I, quickening these, take the plants in my hand — the soul of the disease perishes, as if before a life-snatcher.

sanskrit: yasyauṣadhīḥ prasarpathaṅgam-aṅgam paruṣ-paruḥ | tato yakṣmaṁ vi bādhadhva ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
english: Into whose every limb, every joint, you plants spread — drive out the consumption from him, like a fierce lion resting in the middle.

sanskrit: sākaṁ yakṣma pra pata cāṣeṇa kikidīvinā | sākaṁ vātasya dhrājyā sākaṁ naśya nihākayā ||
english: O consumption, fly away together with the blue jay and the spotted one; fly away with the rush of the wind, together with the downward swoop — perish.

sanskrit: anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata | tāḥ sarvāḥ saṁvidānā idam me prāvatā vacaḥ ||
english: Let one of you help another; let each one aid the next; all of you in agreement — help this my speech.

sanskrit: yāḥ phalinīr yā aphalā apuṣpā yāś ca puṣpiṇīḥ | bṛhaspatiprasūtās tā no muñcantvṁ aṁhasaḥ ||
english: Those that bear fruit and those without fruit, those without flowers and those that flower — prompted by Bṛhaspati, may they free us from distress.

sanskrit: muñcantu mā śapathyād atho varuṇyād uta | atho yamasya paḍbīśāt sarvamad devakilbiṣāt ||
english: May they free me from the curse, and from Varuṇa's bond; from Yama's noose as well, and from all divine transgression.

sanskrit: avapataṇtīr avadan divā oṣadhaya pari | yaṁ jīvam aśnavāmahai na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ ||
english: Flying down, the plants have spoken all around from the sky: that man whom we reach while he is living, he shall not be harmed.

sanskrit: yā oṣadhīḥ somarājñīr bahvīḥ śatavicakṣaṇāḥ | tāsām tvam asy uttamā raraṁ kāmāya śaṁ hṛde ||
english: O you who are the plants, ruled by Soma, many and hundred-eyed — among them you are the highest; I have given you gladly for desire, wholesome to the heart.

sanskrit: yā oṣadhīḥ somarājñīr viṣṭhitāḥ pṛthivīm anu | bṛhaspatiprasūtā asyai saṁ data vīryam ||
english: You plants ruled by Soma, spread all over the earth, prompted by Bṛhaspati — grant your power to this one.

sanskrit: mā vo riṣat khanitā yasmai cāhaṁ khanāmi vaḥ | dvipac catuṣpad asmākaṁ sarvam astv anāturam ||
english: Let not the digger be harmed — he for whom I dig you; may all of ours, two-footed and four-footed, be free from disease.

sanskrit: yāś cedam upaśṛṇvanti yāś ca dūram parāgatāḥ | sarvāḥ saṁgatya vīrudho 'syai saṁ data vīryam ||
english: Those who hear this nearby and those who have come from afar — all the herbs coming together, grant your power to this one.

sanskrit: oṣadhayaḥ saṁ vadante somena saha rājñā | yasmai kṛṇoti brāhmaṇas taṁ rājan pārayāmasi ||
english: The plants speak together with Soma the king: O king, we shall carry across the one for whom the Brahmin prepares us.

sanskrit: tvam uttamāsy oṣadhe tava vṛkṣā upastayaḥ | upastir astu so 'smākaṁ yo asmāṁ abhi dāsati ||
english: You are the highest, O plant; your props are the trees; let him who would oppress us become a prop — a dependent of ours.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate prati me devatām ihi mitro vā yad varuṇo vāsi pūṣā | ādityair vā yad vasubhir marutvān sa parjanyaṁ śaṁtanave vṛṣāya ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, meet the deity on my behalf — whether you be Mitra or Varuṇa or Pūṣan; or whether you be together with the Ādityas, with the Vasus, with the Maruts — let him send rain for Śantanu.

sanskrit: ā devo dūto ajiраś cikitvān tvad devāpe abhi mām agacchat | pratīcīnaḥ prati mām ā vavṛtsva dadhāmi te dyumatīṁ vācam āsan ||
english: O Devāpi, a divine, swift, wise messenger has come to me from you; turn yourself facing toward me; I place a bright speech in your mouth.

sanskrit: asme dhehi dyumatīṁ vācam āsan bṛhaspate anamīvām iṣirām | yayā vṛṣṭiṁ śaṁtanave vanāva divo drapso madhumāṁ ā viveśa ||
english: Set a bright, disease-free, active speech in our mouths, O Bṛhaspati; with which we may win rain for Śantanu — the sweet drop has entered from the sky.

sanskrit: ā no drapsā madhumanto viśantv indra dehy adhirathaṁ sahasram | ni ṣīda hotraṁ ṛtuthā yajasva devān devāpe haviṣā saparya ||
english: Let the sweet drops come to us, O Indra; give us a thousand above the chariot; sit down to the Hotṛ's task, sacrifice in due order, serve the gods with oblation, O Devāpi.

sanskrit: ārṣṭiṣeṇo hotraṁ ṛṣir niṣīdan devāpir devasumatiṁ cikitvān | sa uttarasmād adharaṁ samudram apo divyā asṛjad varṣyā abhi ||
english: Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, the Ṛṣi, sitting in the Hotṛ seat; Devāpi, seeking the goodwill of the gods — he directed the celestial rain-waters from the upper toward the lower sea.

sanskrit: asmin samudre adhy uttarasmin āpo devebhir nivṛtā atiṣṭhan | tā adravann ārṣṭiṣeṇena sṛṣṭā devāpinā preṣitā mṛkṣiṇīṣu ||
english: In this upper sea the waters held back by the gods had stood still; they ran, released by Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, sent forth by Devāpi — upon the oblation-sprinkled ones.

sanskrit: yad devāpiḥ śaṁtanave purohito hotrāya vṛtaḥ kṛpayann adīdhet | devaśrutaṁ vṛṣṭivaniṁ rarāṇo bṛhaspatir vācam asmā ayacchat ||
english: When Devāpi, appointed purohita for Śantanu, having been chosen for the Hotṛ's office, blazed with compassion — Bṛhaspati, bestowing what the gods hear, what wins rain, gave him speech.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvā devāpiḥ śuśucāno agna ārṣṭiṣeṇo manuṣyaḥ samīdhe | viśvebhir devair anumadhyamānaḥ pra parjanyam īrayā vṛṣṭimantam ||
english: You, O Agni, whom Devāpi, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa the human, blazing, has kindled — praised along with all the gods — send forth rain-bringing Parjanya.

sanskrit: tvām pūrva ṛṣayo gīrbhir āyan tvām adhvareṣu puruhūta viśve | sahasrāṇy adhirathāny asme ā no yajñaṁ rohidaśvopa yāhi ||
english: The ancient seers came to you with their hymns; all of them at the rites, O much-invoked one; among us are thousands beyond the chariots — come to our sacrifice, O you with red-roan steeds.

sanskrit: etāny agne navatir nava tve āhutāny adhirathā sahasrā | tebhir vardhasva tanvaḥ śūra pūrvīr divo no vṛṣṭim iṣito rirīhi ||
english: O Agni, ninety-nine oblations beyond the chariot, thousands, have been offered to you; with them grow in many bodies, O hero — impelled, release the rain from the sky for us.

sanskrit: etāny agne navatiṁ sahasrā sam pra yaccha vṛṣṇa indrāya bhāgam | vidvān patha ṛtuśo devayānān apy aulānaṁ divi deveṣu dhehi ||
english: O Agni, present these ninety thousand together as the share for Indra the bull; knowing the paths seasonally trodden by the gods, place Aulāna among the gods in the sky.

sanskrit: agne bādhasva vi mṛdho vi durgahāpāmīvām apa rakṣāṁsi sedha | asmāt samudrād bṛhato divo no 'pāṁ bhūmānam upa naḥ sṛjeha ||
english: O Agni, drive away the destroyers, drive away the hard-to-conquer; drive away disease, drive away the demons; from this great sea of the sky send the fullness of waters to us here.

sanskrit: kaṁ naś citram iṣaṇyasi cikitvān pṛthumānaṁ vāśraṁ vāvṛdhadhyai | kat tasya dātu śavaso vyuṣṭau takṣad vajraṁ vṛtraturaw apinvat ||
english: What wonder do you impel for us, O wise one, to make the far-reaching cry grow? What at the dawning of his might shall he bestow? He shaped the bolt, the Vṛtra-slayer, he swelled it with power.

sanskrit: sa hi dyutā vidyutā veti sāma pṛthuṁ yonim asuratvā sasāda | sa sanīḻebhiḥ prasahāno asya bhrātur na ṛte saptamasya māyāḥ ||
english: For he advances with lightning's flash pursuing the chant; by his asura-power he has sat in the broad womb; he, overpowering with nestlings, without the tricks of the seventh brother of his.

sanskrit: sa vājaṁ yātāpaduṣpadāyan svarṣātā pari ṣadat saniṣyan | anarvā yac chatadhurasya vedo ghnaṁ chiśnadevan abhi varpasā bhūt ||
english: He went for the prize; making ill-footed ones good-footed, the sun-winner sat down going to win; un-rivalled when he found the wealth of the hundred-shafted one — the phallus-gods he smote, he overpowered with his form.

sanskrit: sa yahviyo avanīr goṣv arvā juhoti pradhanyāsu sasriḥ | apādo yatra yujyāso arathā droṇyaśvāsa īrate ghṛtaṁ vāḥ ||
english: He, the swift bull, pours into the great rivers, into the cows — running foremost in contests; where the footless, chariotless ones are yoked, the trough-horses set the ghee in motion.

sanskrit: sa rudrebhir aśastavāra ṛbhvā hitvī gayam āreavadya āgāt | vamrasya manye mithuṇā vivāvrī annam abhītyārodayan muṣāyan ||
english: He, with the Rudras who bar evil, skilled, having left his home, came to the blameless; I believe that the two insects uncovered coupled, having seized food, causing it to ascend through plunder.

sanskrit: sa id dāsaṁ tuvīravam patir dan ṣaḷakṣaṁ triśīrṣāṇaṁ damanyat | asya trito nv ojasā vṛdhāno vipā varāham ayoagrayā han ||
english: The lord, having given the loud-roaring Dāsa, the six-eyed, three-headed one, subdued him; Trita, now strengthened by his strength, struck the boar with his iron-tipped spear.

sanskrit: sa druhvaṇe manuṣa ūrdhvasāna ā sāviṣad arśasānāya śarum | sa nṛtamo nahuṣo smat sujātaḥ puro bhinad arhan dasyuhatye ||
english: He, with upraised arrow, shot a dart for the man who injures — against the tormenter; he, the most manly, Nahuṣa, well-born among us, broke open the forts in worthy Dasyu-slaying.

sanskrit: so abhriyyo na yavasa udanyaṁ kṣayāya gātuṁ vidan no asme | upa yat sīdad induṁ śarīraiḥ śyeno ayopāṣṭir hanti dasyūn ||
english: He, like a cloud finding pasture and water, found the way to dwelling, not for us; when the Soma-drop settled with his body — the hawk, Ayopāṣṭi, strikes the Dasyus.

sanskrit: sa vrādhathaḥ śavasānebhir asya kutsāya śuṣṇaṁ kṛpaṇe parādāt | ayaṁ kavim anayac chasyamānam atkaṁ yo asya sanito ta nṛṇām ||
english: He who grew in power through his mighty acts gave Śuṣṇa to Kutsa in the miser's place; this one led the celebrated seer — he who is the winner of the cloak and of men.

sanskrit: ayaṁ daśasyan naryebhir asya dasmo devebhir varuṇo na māyī | ayaṁ kanīna ṛtupā avedy amimītāraruṁ yaś catuṣpāt ||
english: This one, worshipping with his manly helpers, the wonder-worker like Varuṇa with the gods, the magician; this young one, the time-observant, is found — he who measured out the four-footed, restless one.

sanskrit: asya stomebhir auśija ṛjiśvā vrajaṁ darayad vṛṣabheṇa pipro ḥ | sutvā yad yajato dīdayad gīḥ purā iyāno abhi varpasā bhūt ||
english: By his hymns, Ṛjiśvā the Auśija burst open the fold with Pipru's bull; when the adorable Soma-presser made his song shine, he advanced, becoming manifest in his form.

sanskrit: evā maho asura vakṣathāya vamrakaḥ paḍbhir upa sarpad indram | sa iyānaḥ karati svastim asmā iṣam ūrjaṁ sukṣitiṁ viśvam ābhāḥ ||
english: Thus, O Asura, for the growth of the great one, the ant has crept up to Indra on his feet; he going thus shall make well-being for him — food, vigour, good dwelling, all-illumining.

sanskrit: indra dṛhya maghavan tvāvad id bhuja iha stutaḥ sutapā bodhi no vṛdhe | devebhir naḥ savitā prāvatu śrutam ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: O Indra, hold firm, O bountiful one — only so great an enjoyment; praised here, you who drink the pressed Soma well, be for our growth; let Savitṛ further our famous prayer with the gods — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: bharāya su bharata bhāgam ṛtviyam pra vāyave śucipe krandadiṣṭaye | gaurasya yaḥ payasaḥ pītim ānaśa ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Carry well the seasonally due share for the bearer; forth to Vāyu, the pure drinker, for the cry of desire; he who has obtained the drinking of the Gaura's milk — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: ā no devaḥ savitā sāviṣad vaya ṛjūyate yajamānāya sunvate | yathā devān pratibhūṣema pākavad ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: May the god Savitṛ send us life-force to the straight-going sacrificer who presses Soma; so that we may serve the gods like the simple-hearted — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: indro asme sumanā astu viśvahā rājā somaḥ suvitasyādhy etu naḥ | yathā-yathā mitradhi tāni saṁdadhur ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: May Indra be benevolent to us always; may King Soma come over to us for our well-being; just as they have joined together what belongs to Mitra — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: indra ukthena śavasā paror dadhe bṛhaspate pratarītāsy āyuṣaḥ | yajño manuḥ pramatiś naḥ pitā hi kam ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Indra with his recitation and strength has been established before; O Bṛhaspati, you are the extender of life-span; the sacrifice is Manu, Pramati is our dear father — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: indrasya nu sukṛtaṁ daivyaṁ saho 'gnir gṛhe jaritā medhiraḥ kaviḥ | yajñaś ca bhūd vidathe cāru rantama ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Indra's divine strength of well-doing; Agni in the house, the praising wise seer; may the sacrifice become the most beautiful delight in the assembly — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: na vo guhā cakṛma bhūri duṣkṛtaṁ nāviṣṭyaṁ vasavo deva heḻanam | mākir no devā anṛtasya varpasa ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: We have not done much wrong in secret, no offence manifest to you, O Vasus, O gods; let no deity through the form of untruth — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: apāmīvāṁ savitā sāviṣan nyag varīya id apa sedhanty adrayaḥ | grāvā yatra madhusud ucyate bṛhad ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Savitṛ has sent disease downward; the rocks drive away what is wider downward; where the pressing-stone is called the great Soma-sweeter — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo grāvā vasavo astu sotari viśvā dveṣāṁsi sanutar yuyota | sa no devaḥ savitā pāyur īḍya ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Let the pressing-stone stand upright, O Vasus, for the presser; keep all hatreds far away; may that god Savitṛ, the praiseworthy protector, be for us — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: ūrjaṁ gāvo yavase pīvo attana ṛtasya yāḥ sadane kośe aṅgdhve | tanūr eva tanvo astu bheṣajam ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Let the cows eat vigour and fat in the pasture; you who touch the treasure in the seat of Ṛta — let the body's medicine belong to the body — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: kratuprāvā jaritā śaśvatām ava indra id bhadrā pramatiḥ sutāvatām | pūrṇam ūdhar divyaṁ yasya siktaya ā sarvatātim aditiṁ vṛṇīmahe ||
english: The will-sustaining singer has always been sheltered by Indra alone — the good Pramati of the Soma-pressers; whose streams are the full heavenly udder — we choose Aditi, the all-encompassing.

sanskrit: citras te bhānuḥ kratuprā abhiṣṭiḥ santi spṛdho jaraṇiprā adhṛṣṭāḥ | rajiṣṭhayā rajyā paśva ā gos tūtūrṣati pary agraṁ duvasyuḥ ||
english: Wondrous is your brilliance, your victory that fills the will; there are irresistible rivals that fill the praise; by the straightest course, by the right, toward cattle, toward the cow — the eager worshipper strives to surpass all.
